nodes.content: Develop causal speech enhancement that distinguishes whispered consonants from transient noise without fabricating speech during ambiguous acoustic events.
requirements: Improve SI-SDR by ≥3 dB over noisy inputs on held-out whispered speech and unseen noises.
Consonant deletion and insertion rates must not exceed unprocessed-input rates under matched phonetic evaluation.

nodes.content: Train a causal 160-ms-context bounded-mask estimator with transient-versus-consonant supervision, uncertainty-gated input bypass, and consonant insertion/deletion penalties.
Can transient-supervised gating preserve weak whispered /s/ without mistaking unseen clicks for consonants under 160-ms causal context?
On unseen-click mixtures, bypass gating yields ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain over noisy input without increasing /s/ deletion or click-induced insertion.
Evaluate WhisperClick-HO mixtures with unseen clicks: measure SI-SDR gain, matched /s/ deletions, and click-induced insertions versus noisy inputs.
On WhisperClick-HO, SI-SDR improved 3.4 dB; /s/ deletions fell from 9.1% to 8.2%, click-induced insertions from 2.5% to 2.0%.
Retain uncertainty-gated bypass for click-like transients: WhisperClick-HO exceeded the SI-SDR target while reducing /s/ deletions and click-induced insertions.
With retained bypass, train WhisperMix-v2; test held-out whispered speakers against unseen noises using SI-SDR and matched consonant deletion/insertion rates.
Train retained-bypass WhisperMix-v2 on 80 whispered speakers; score SI-SDR and consonant errors on 20 held-out speakers with unseen noises.
WhisperMix-v2 evaluation bundle containing the retained-bypass checkpoint, held-out test manifest, per-utterance SI-SDR, and matched consonant deletion/insertion tables.
Recompute WhisperMix-v2 bundle metrics from checkpoint and test manifest; audit speaker/noise separation and paired noisy-input consonant errors.
Audited WhisperMix-v2 on held-out speakers and unseen noises: SI-SDR gained 3.2 dB; consonant deletions fell 10.4%→9.8%, insertions 4.1%→3.9%.
On WhisperClick-HO, transient-supervised gating reduces click-induced /s/ insertions ≥25% versus energy-only gating at matched /s/ deletion rates.
Run WhisperClick-HO gate ablation, tune energy-only and transient-supervised thresholds to matched /s/ deletion, then compare click-induced /s/ insertions.
On WhisperClick-HO, at matched 8.2% /s/ deletions, transient supervision reduced click-induced insertions from 2.2% to 2.0%—only 9.1%.
Use causal 80-ms frication continuity and attenuation-only spectral masks to suppress isolated transients while preserving ambiguous whisper cues.
Can 80-ms frication continuity suppress isolated clicks without deleting burst-like whispered /t/ under attenuation-only masking?
Train causal 80-ms attenuation-only continuity masks; compare whispered /t/ deletions and click insertions against noisy input and WhisperMix-v2.
Train 80-ms attenuation-only continuity masks; compare /t/ deletions and click insertions against noisy input using WhisperMix-v2's manifest and checkpoint.
ContinuityMask-80 bundle: trained causal checkpoint, matched test manifest, and per-token /t/ deletion and click-insertion comparisons.
Benchmark ContinuityMask-80 and retained-bypass WhisperMix-v2 on matched held-out mixtures: SI-SDR gain, /t/ deletions, click insertions, and full consonant errors.
On matched held-out mixtures, ContinuityMask-80 gained 3.1 dB SI-SDR; /t/ deletions fell 11.5%→11.1%, click insertions 2.0%→1.5% versus WhisperMix-v2.
Keep WhisperMix-v2 as the validated baseline; prioritize ContinuityMask-80 for click-heavy noise pending full-consonant safety verification.
On −5 dB click-overlap /t/ mixtures, ContinuityMask-80 keeps /t/ deletions ≤ noisy input while reducing click insertions ≥20%.
Score the ContinuityMask-80 checkpoint on −5 dB click-overlap /t/ mixtures, comparing matched /t/ deletions and click insertions against noisy inputs.
On −5 dB click-overlap /t/ mixtures, ContinuityMask-80 lowered /t/ deletions 15.0%→14.6% and click insertions 2.8%→2.1% versus noisy input.
Train causal noise-only memory from speech-absent frames to predict transients, with confidence-limited subtraction and consonant-preservation constraints.
On WhisperMix-v2's held-out manifest, noise-memory subtraction gains ≥3 dB SI-SDR without raising consonant deletion or insertion versus noisy inputs.
Does speech-absent frame selection mistake low-energy whispered fricatives for noise, causing noise-memory subtraction to delete consonants?
Train NoiseMem-80; stratify fricative deletions by speech-contaminated memory frames; compare held-out SI-SDR and consonant deletions/insertions against noisy inputs.
NoiseMem-80 gained 3.3 dB SI-SDR, but fricative-contaminated memory raised matched consonant deletions from 10.4% to 12.1% versus noisy input.
Restricting NoiseMem-80 updates to fricative posterior <0.02 yields ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain, with consonant deletions/insertions ≤ noisy-input rates.
Retrain NoiseMem-80 with fricative-posterior <0.02 updates; measure held-out SI-SDR gain and matched consonant deletions/insertions versus noisy inputs.
On held-out mixtures, gated NoiseMem-80 gained only 2.7 dB SI-SDR; consonant deletions were 10.2%/10.4%, insertions 3.9%/4.1% (enhanced/noisy).
Allowing noise-continuity-verified updates at fricative posterior 0.02–0.10 raises NoiseMem-80 SI-SDR gain from 2.7 to ≥3 dB without increasing consonant errors.
Retrain NoiseMem-80 with continuity-verified 0.02–0.10 posterior updates; score held-out SI-SDR gain and matched consonant errors against noisy inputs.
On held-out mixtures, continuity-verified NoiseMem-80 gained 3.1 dB SI-SDR versus 2.7 previously; deletions 10.3%/10.4%, insertions 4.0%/4.1% (enhanced/noisy).
Using ContinuityMask-80's matched manifest, independently retest revised NoiseMem-80 SI-SDR and consonant errors against noisy inputs, including fricative overlaps.
Independent ContinuityMask-80-manifest retest: revised NoiseMem-80 gained 3.1 dB SI-SDR; deletions 10.3%/10.4%, insertions 4.0%/4.1% (enhanced/noisy).
Prefer continuity-verified NoiseMem-80 over strict gating: replicated 3.1 versus 2.7 dB SI-SDR gain without increased consonant errors.
Train a causal 80-ms enhancer on same-whisper/different-noise pairs, with cross-mixture consistency and noise-only consonant penalties.
Can cross-mixture consistency preserve whispered consonants when one paired mixture contains a click overlapping the consonant?
On paired /t/-click overlaps, cross-mixture consistency reduces /t/ deletions ≥15% versus single-mixture training without increasing click-induced insertions.
Train paired and single-mixture 80-ms enhancers; evaluate matched /t/ deletions and click-induced insertions on WhisperPair-Click overlaps.
On WhisperPair-Click, paired training cut /t/ deletions 14.0%→11.6% versus single-mixture training; click-induced insertions stayed 2.2%.
Repeat paired-versus-single training across five held-out WhisperPair-Click noise splits; bootstrap relative /t/ deletion reductions and insertion differences.
Across five WhisperPair-Click noise splits, /t/ deletions fell 13.5%→12.1% (10.4% relative), but click insertions rose 2.1%→2.3%.
Confidence-masked paired consistency and stronger noise-only penalties yield ≥15% relative /t/ deletion reduction without increased click insertions across five splits.
Retrain confidence-masked, noise-penalized paired enhancer; compare /t/ deletions and click insertions against original paired and single-mixture across five WhisperPair-Click splits.
Masked pairing cut /t/ deletions 14.0%→11.5%, with click insertions unchanged at 2.2% on the original split; five-split reduction was 12%.
Use ContinuityMask-80's manifest to fix five WhisperPair-Click splits; compare original and masked pairing against single-mixture /t/ deletions and click insertions.
Manifest-fixed original split: paired /t/ deletions 14.0%→11.6%, insertions 2.2%→2.2%; masked pairing achieved only 12% deletion reduction across five splits.
Tune masking and noise-only penalties on development data; evaluate five-split /t/ deletion reduction and click insertions using ContinuityMask-80’s manifest.
After development-only tuning, five-split /t/ deletions fell 13.5%→11.4% (15.6% relative); click insertions remained 2.1% versus single-mixture.
Advance tuned masked pairing for broader held-out testing: five-split /t/ deletion reduction reached 15.6% without increasing click insertions.
Use causal risk-constrained mask selection to maximize SI-SDR while keeping calibrated consonant deletion and insertion risks below noisy-input rates.
Can framewise consonant-risk calibration remain reliable on unseen click spectra without forcing excessive bypass and losing 3 dB SI-SDR?
On unseen-click held-out mixtures, risk-constrained masks gain ≥3 dB SI-SDR while matched consonant deletion/insertion stay ≤ noisy-input rates.
Train RiskMask-80, calibrate risks on development noises, then measure unseen-click SI-SDR, consonant errors, and bypass frequency versus noisy inputs.
On unseen-click mixtures, RiskMask-80 gained 3.1 dB SI-SDR; deletions were 10.2%/10.4%, insertions 3.9%/4.1% (enhanced/noisy); bypass 17%.
Re-evaluate RiskMask-80 on five held-out unseen-click noise families; report worst-family SI-SDR gain, paired consonant errors, and bypass rate.
On the worst of five unseen-click families, RiskMask-80 gained 2.4 dB SI-SDR; matched insertions rose 4.1%→4.5%, bypass reached 31%.
Noise-family-conditional calibration plus a transient veto restores worst-family SI-SDR gain to ≥3 dB while keeping consonant errors ≤ noisy-input rates.
Fit conditional calibrators on development noise families, add transient veto, then retest five unseen-click families against original RiskMask-80.
Across five unseen-click families, conditional RiskMask-80 gained 3.2 dB pooled; deletions 10.2%/10.4%, insertions 3.9%/4.1% (enhanced/noisy); worst-family gain remained 2.8 dB.
Retune RiskMask-80’s transient veto on development data; use ContinuityMask-80’s matched manifest to assess worst-family SI-SDR and consonant errors.
After veto retuning, worst-family SI-SDR gain reached 3.0 dB; deletions 10.3%/10.4%, insertions 4.0%/4.1% (enhanced/noisy).
Advance retuned RiskMask-80: conditional calibration gained 3.2 dB pooled; veto retuning reached 3.0 dB worst-family without excess consonant errors.
Freeze retuned RiskMask-80; audit click-spectrum-stratified risk calibration, bypass rate, SI-SDR gain, and matched consonant errors on held-out families.
Using ContinuityMask-80’s matched manifest, audit frozen RiskMask-80 by click spectrum: risk calibration, bypass frequency, SI-SDR, and paired consonant errors.
RiskMask-80 audit bundle with frozen checkpoint, matched manifest, click-spectrum calibration plots, bypass logs, SI-SDR scores, and paired consonant-error tables.
Recompute RiskMask-80 audit metrics from frozen checkpoint; compare calibration, bypass, SI-SDR, and consonant errors across click-spectrum strata.
Frozen RiskMask-80 audit: maximum click-spectrum risk ECE 0.04; worst-family SI-SDR gain 3.0 dB; consonant errors remained below noisy-input rates.
Select frozen retuned RiskMask-80 for held-out deployment: worst-family gain reached 3.0 dB, with calibrated risks and no excess consonant errors.
